That completes all nine areas you asked me to settle. Here's the full picture that's now approved (24 behaviour scenarios in all):

**Saving** — auto-filled title/description/icon/preview image (editable), only the link required; tag suggestions; private Markdown notes; no duplicates (on save or edit); recover when a page can't be fetched; reject non-addresses.

**Finding** — one live, case-insensitive search across everything; a query language (`#tag` exact, AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, `"phrases"`, quoted operators as text); click-a-tag to filter; note excerpts explaining note-only matches; reusable saved searches.

**Reading state** — save-to-read-later choice; All / To read / Finished tabs; mark finished / move back, never deleting.

**Managing** — permanent delete (with confirmation) vs. reversible archive (hidden, restorable); bulk select (including whole current view) to tag/untag, mark, archive, delete, with tag suggestions; sorting by date or title.

**Keeping** — automatic preserved copy per bookmark (self-contained page, or the PDF by real file type), retry on failure, optional Internet Archive submission.

**Portability & display** — import/export the standard browser-bookmarks file (titles, tags, original dates preserved; imports arrive as reference); display preferences for default sort, items shown, and text size.

**Deferred to later versions** (noted): automatic dead-link detection, and visual/look-and-feel polish.

Everything above has been demonstrated and confirmed by you, and the interaction methods are settled.

**May I now switch from exploring to building this as the real application?** On your approval I'll begin Phase 2 — implementing this approved scope for real (fresh implementation driven by the approved behaviours, not the prototype code).
